To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Transmission through a beam-modified absorber is not only a function of beam energy and absorbers thickness but also depends upon field size, location of the source and absorber, and the point at which the transmission is measured.
the narrow beam transmission calculations for a field-modifying absorber can be improved by incorporating the scatter component generated by the absorbers.
the narrow beam attenuation coefficients are not sufficient to predict broad beam transmission, and scatter is an important component of transmission.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a method to calculate effective transmission through beam-modifying absorvers and to calculate scattered radiation generated by these absorbers.
the effects of scatter generated by a beam modifying absorber in a high energy photon beam.
the development of a method to calculate the transmission through arbitrarily shaped absorbers, which can be used for treatment planning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
narrow beam calculations are not suitable for predicting transmission of a megavoltage photon beam through beam-modifying absorpers.
scatter generated by a beam-modifying attenuator is a significant factor in the transmission of a beam.
the narrow beam attenuation coefficients are not sufficient to describe the transmission of megavoltage beams through beam-modifying absorpers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
scatter due to beam-modifying absorbs has a significant effect on the transmission through the absorber and the dose at the treatment point.
scatter generated by beam modifiers is a function of the absorber material, beam energy, and field size.

the narrow beam transmission calculations are inadequate for the calculation of transmission through a beam-modified absorber and the scatter generated by an absorber is an important component of the transmission.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the scatter component in the transmitted beam should not be neglected, especially for small fields and for beams of higher energies.
, for accurate dosimetry in photon beams, one should use a method that accounts for scatter from beam-modifying absorpers, and not rely on narrow beam attenuation coefficients.
the scatter component of the transmitted radiation is a significant contributor to transmission measurements and cannot be ignored.
